title: Section-normalized consecutive scalar square for fixed realization
statement: Let f:Z→X be a scheme morphism and d an adic coefficient datum on A [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Write B_n for the completion quotient and q_n:B_(n+1)→B_n [def-weil-pbc-lisse-tower-etale-descent-data]. Define the ordinary fixed realization F_n by restriction along A/I^(n+1)→B_n followed by the prescribed associated-module-sheaf functor on Z. There exists a unique isomorphism c_n:Res(q_n) followed by F_(n+1) ≅ F_n followed by restriction along the actual pulled quotient map for which the underlying abelian-sheaf map is the identity after the canonical abelian sheafification counits. These counits define the predicate LisseTowerScalarSquareSections; it fixes c_n uniquely. Localize this square, compose with the comparison coefficient square and the fixed composition comparisons, obtaining lisseTowerEtaleScalarIso. For any adic tower M [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower], bounded etale B_(n+1)- and B_n-complexes C,Cprime, and supplied level comparison isomorphisms e,eprime to the pulled actual levels M_(n+1),M_n, any arrow delta:C→Res(q_n)Cprime whose realized arrow, followed by the derived square and Res(eprime), equals e followed by the actual restricted transition has universal etaleIsomorphismNormalizationArrow on every etale Z-object V [def-weil-pbc-derived-normalization-arrows, def-weil-pbc-etale-universal-normalization]. This is LisseTowerScalarSquareReflects. In addition, every universal algebraic arrow k:E→Res(q_n)Eprime has a universal constant normalization arrow after the same etale restriction, as specified by LisseTowerConstantLocalUniversal. No descended transition, further local realization, restriction-coherence equation or stalk assertion is constructed.

proof.text: The completion quotient homomorphisms commute with consecutive quotients. Apply naturality of pbcLevelConstantComparison and of proEtaleConstantInverseImageMap to prove the actual scalar-presentation square. For a commutative square of constant ring presentations, restrict the lower module-sheafification unit along the upper action and extend by the module-sheafification adjunction. Forgetting scalars identifies this map with the identity of abelian sheafification, so it is invertible and natural. Whisker with the presheaf scalar-composition isomorphism to obtain the required ordinary square. The abelian sheafification counits prove its section normalization; faithfulness and cancellation of these counits prove uniqueness. The section equation is first proved over abstract coefficient presentations. Proved equalities identify these formulas with the unchanged public forgetful comparisons of the item, so specializing it never expands the concrete adic coefficient objects into a component calculation.

An invertible inverse scalar mate sends an initial structured arrow to an initial structured arrow: identify the given arrow with its scalar-adjunction unit, compose the mate with the target isomorphism, and use the mate unit identity. Apply this elementary categorical calculation to the already proved inverseImage_mate_isIso in ConstantAdicQuotientScalarComparison. The original tower transition is the scalar unit followed by its supplied normalization isomorphism. Hence its actual restricted transition is universal.

Localize the constructed ordinary scalar square using mapDerivedCategorySquareIso and the fixed realization composition comparisons. The supplied descent equation, after expanding lisseTowerEtaleScalarIso, is precisely its composite with the comparison coefficient square. Conjugating by e and eprime transports the universality just proved to the realized compared delta. Both fixed derived realization functors are equivalences, so StructuredArrow.map₂ is an equivalence and reflects initiality. Thus the compared delta is universal. Apply comparisonNormalization_reflects_universal and then etaleSourceNormalization_universal to obtain the required arrow on every etale source. Only the two latter tensor statements remain unproved in this delivery.

For the final conjunct, apply the already proved normalizationConstantArrow_isUniversal to the supplied algebraically universal arrow. Apply the same etaleSourceNormalization_universal to this constant arrow. Combine existence, sections, the reflected universality, this constant universality, and section uniqueness to prove the unchanged exists-unique statement.

lean.statement:
theorem lisseTower_scalar_restriction {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ X)
    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃! c : LisseTowerScalarSquare f d n,
      LisseTowerScalarSquareSections f d n c ∧ LisseTowerScalarSquareReflects f d n c ∧
        LisseTowerConstantLocalUniversal Z d n
